{{nihongo|'''Ikoma Shrine'''|往馬坐伊古麻都比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Ikoma-ni-imasu Ikomatsuhiko Shrine''' (いこまにいますいこまつひこじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Ikoma, Nara|Q328610|qid=Q328610}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. It is commonly known as '''Ikoma Taisha'''.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Principal deities – Ikomatsuhiko-no-Kami (deity of {{ill|Mount Ikoma|Q996259|qid=Q996259}}), Ikomatsuhime-no-Kami (deity of Mount Ikoma), Okinaga Tarashihime no Mikoto ({{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}), Ashinaka Tsuhiko no Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971}}), Hondawake no Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuragi no Taka-nukahime no Mikoto}} (mother of Empress Jingū), and Okinaga no Sukune no Ōkimi no Mikoto (father of Empress Jingū)

Ikomatsuhiko-no-Kami and Ikomatsuhime-no-Kami have been worshipped since ancient times as deities governing fire. The fire-drill wood (hikiri-gi) used to kindle the sacred fire for the {{ill|Daijosai|Q11433653|qid=Q11433653}} has traditionally been presented by this shrine, and the shrine’s fire-drill wood was also used for the Daijōsai of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Akihito}}. Texts such as the *Hokuzanshō*, *Gengōki*, and *Kisōki* refer to the shrine’s deity as the “Hikiri-gi no Kami” (God of the Fire-Drill Wood). When determining the two provinces of Yuki and Suki for the Daijōsai (the ritual in which newly harvested rice is first offered to the deities at an imperial accession), divination is performed by burning a turtle shell, and it was customary to use fire-drill wood presented from the Ikoma Shrine on that occasion. This fire-drill wood is called hahaka, corresponding to what is today known as Uwamisozakura (Prunus grayana). The annual festival held on the second Sunday of October (formerly {{ill|October 10|Q2921|qid=Q2921}}) is called the “Fire Deity Festival,” and together with the Wind Deity Festival of {{ill|Tatsuta Taisha|Q246455|qid=Q246455}} and the Ōimi Festival of {{ill|Hirose Taisha|Q705281|qid=Q705281}}, it has been revered by the imperial court since ancient times. The Fire Deity Festival is a traditional event in which young men carrying torches race down stone steps, and it has been designated an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Intangible Folk Cultural Property}} by the Nara Prefectural Board of Education.

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown, but the shrine has been enshrined at this location as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} (tutelary deity) of the seventeen villages of the Ikoma Valley. Along with {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|Q705542|qid=Q705542}} and {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|Q708859|qid=Q708859}}, it is one of Japan’s leading ancient shrines that enshrine a kannabi ({{ill|Mount Ikoma|Q996259|qid=Q996259}}) as the sacred object of worship within {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. The sacred grove (chinju no mori) covering the shrine grounds is designated a {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}} of Nara Prefecture.

The oldest literary reference appears in the *Sōkoku Fudoki*, in the entry for the 3rd year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} ({{ill|458|Q30922|qid=Q30922}}), which mentions “Ikomatsuhiko Shrine.” In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as “Ikoma-ni-imasu Ikomatsuhiko Shrine, two seats” in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}, {{ill|Heguri district|ja|平群郡|zh|平群郡|qid=Q11483501}}, ranked as a major shrine and recorded as receiving offerings at the Tsukinami and Niiname festivals. Of the two seats of Ikoma-ni-imasu Ikomatsuhiko Shrine, one also received offerings for prayers for rain.

During the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, there were said to be eleven {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} (temple-shrine complexes).

Originally, the main hall enshrined two seats as the tutelary deities of the land, but in the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, devotion to {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}}, the guardian deity of the warrior class, flourished, and five Hachiman deities were enshrined together, resulting in the present seven seats.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}, due to the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, the jingū-ji were abolished and the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}.

=== Shrine precincts ===
* Main halls (7 buildings) – Seven connected {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|Q3193781|qid=Q3193781}} cypress-bark-roofed main halls stand here. Ikomatsuhiko-no-Kami is enshrined at the center, with Ikomatsuhime-no-Kami to the right. From the left, the order is: Okinaga no Sukune no Ōkimi no Mikoto, Okinaga Tarashihime no Mikoto ({{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}), Hondawake no Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}), Ikomatsuhiko-no-Kami, Ikomatsuhime-no-Kami, Ashinaka Tsuhiko no Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971}}), and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuragi no Taka-nukahime no Mikoto}}.
* Norito hall
* Worship hall (haiden)
* Eireiden – It is said that a golden memorial tablet of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Empress Shōtoku}} was buried at this site.
* Kannon Hall – A remnant of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}. It enshrines a statue of {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|Q11404731|qid=Q11404731}} (traditionally attributed to Unkei), the honji-butsu of Empress Jingū. Few shrines retain Buddhist halls.
* Offering hall (shinsenjo)
* Purification hall (saikan)
* Ritual implements storehouse
* Rōmon gate – In fact, it is a karamon gate.
* Yakura
* Kōza
* North seat
* South seat
* Gagaku hall
* Misogi place
* North mikoshi storehouse
* South mikoshi storehouse
* Shrine office
